text: α2-Chimaerin, a Rac-specific GTPase-activating protein (RacGAP) isoform, refines dendritic spine morphology during late postnatal development, thereby determining adult spine features. In mice with global and conditional α-chimaerin knock-out, disrupting α2-chimaerin—but not α1-chimaerin—increased hippocampal spine size and density, while overexpressing α2-chimaerin in developing hippocampal neurons decreased spine size. α2-Chimaerin disruption also suppressed EphA-mediated spine morphogenesis in cultured developing neurons. Juvenile-stage α2-chimaerin deletion increased adult hippocampal spine size and contextual fear learning; adult-only deletion left spine morphology and contextual learning unaltered. Thus developmental α2-chimaerin signaling determines adult spine morphology and normal cognitive ability.
